title: 2003 AMC 12A Problem 10
statement: Al, Bert, and Carl are the winners of a school drawing for a pile of Halloween candy, which they are to divide in a ratio of \(3 : 2 : 1,\) respectively. Due to some confusion they come at different times to claim their prizes, and each assumes he is the first to arrive. If each takes what he believes to be his correct share of candy, what fraction of the candy goes unclaimed?

solutions.text:
The shares are \(\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac16\) of the pile.

Each person assumes he is first, so Al leaves \(\dfrac12,\) Bert leaves \(\dfrac23,\) and Carl leaves \(\dfrac56\) of the candy present when he arrives.

The unclaimed fraction is \(\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac56=\dfrac{5}{18},\) regardless of the order.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The three shares are \(\dfrac12,\dfrac13,\dfrac16\) of the whole
Each person leaves a fixed fraction of whatever candy is present, so the order does not matter
